title: Sogroya Becomes First Once-Weekly Growth Hormone Approved for Turner Syndrome in the U.S.
summary:
The FDA has approved Novo Nordisk's once-weekly growth hormone Sogroya, or somapacitan-beco, for growth failure in children with Turner syndrome ages 2.5 and older. Contemporary Pediatrics reported Nov. 20. Novo Nordisk says it is the first long-acting growth hormone approved for this use.

Until now, girls with Turner syndrome who needed growth hormone in the U.S. received daily injections, often for years. Sogroya is given once a week and comes in 5, 10, and 15 mg pens.

title: FDA nod to first treatment for neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease
summary:
The US FDA has approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets, marking a major breakthrough in the treatment of Type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3). 

It is the first treatment specifically approved for the neurological symptoms of the rare inherited disorder in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg.

The drug is designed to cross the blood-brain barrier, targeting the accumulation of harmful substances in the brain — a key driver of the neurological complications associated with GD3.

Overview

 The FDA has approved obinutuzumab (Gazyva) as the first on-label therapy for adults with primary membranous nephropathy (PMN) at risk of disease progression. In a phase 3 trial, 36% of patients achieved complete proteinuria remission compared to 6% receiving tacrolimus. This provides a targeted treatment for a rare autoimmune disease where 30% of untreated cases progress to kidney failure within 10 years.

title: FDA Approves Infilbray, First Pill for the Brain Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher | GoodBad
summary:
